raw_lines: • Most reliability comes from the harness
• The harness, not the model, is the control system
• Optimize for trust, not raw speed
Module 1 Code Lab: Pre-Hook Interception & Loop Detection
• [Lines 8-10] Pre-Execution Interception: Regex matches against destructive commands (rm -rf, sudo) and raises PermissionError before subprocess creation.
• [Lines 15-18] Loop Detector: Sliding-window tracks recent command history and raises RuntimeError after max_retries, halting infinite retry loops.
• Verified Execution: Un-harnessed agent deletes var/log/app.log and loops indefinitely; harnessed agent halts safely with log_survived=True.
What is an Agent Skill? Standard Architecture & Directory Structure
• Modular Agent Capability: An Agent Skill is a self-contained folder providing specialized domain instructions, automated scripts, reference guides, and templates for Claude Code and coding agents.
• Progressive Disclosure: To conserve prompt tokens, the agent only loads YAML metadata from SKILL.md during startup. Heavy scripts and reference docs are loaded into context only when triggered.
├── SKILL.md                # REQUIRED: Entry point, metadata & prompt rules
├── scripts/                # OPTIONAL: Code files the agent can execute
├── references/             # OPTIONAL: Knowledge docs, guides & API schemas
• Discovery Priority: Discovered project-wide in .claude/skills/, module-level in course_implementation/module_XX/skills/, and user-level in ~/.claude/skills/.
Skill Description: Intercepts destructive shell commands and breaks repeating execution retry loops before token waste or data loss occurs.
• When to Use: Running untrusted or automated agent command loops, auditing shell tool calls, or debugging stuck test-fix iterations.
• How to Use: pre_execution_hook(command) regex blocks rm -rf/sudo; loop_detector(command) halts identical retries >= max_retries.
• Five pillars of a production harness
• Policy is code, not a prompt
• Feed pytest failures back to the agent
• Log every tool event to JSONL
Module 2 Code Lab: Tool Scoping, Path Sandboxing & Post-Edit Hook
• [Lines 4-5] Tool Permission Allowlist: Replaces unconstrained agent capabilities with an explicit allowed tool registry.
• [Lines 11-13] Path Sandboxing: Uses Path.resolve().is_relative_to() to prevent directory traversal (../) and external access.
• [Lines 19-20] Post-Edit Secret Scan: Inspects proposed code edits for hardcoded API keys (sk-proj-) before writing to disk.
• Audit Observability: All tool requests and hook decisions are logged to events.jsonl with ISO timestamps.
Skill Description: Enforces least-privilege tool allowlists, path sandboxing via is_relative_to(), post-edit secret scanning, and append-only event tracing.
• When to Use: Sandboxing agent tool invocations, setting up file system isolation, or establishing audit trails in events.jsonl.
• How to Use: validate_tool_permission() checks allowlist & is_relative_to(); run_post_edit_hook() scans for sk-proj-/AKIA keys.
• Vague: make it fast and safe
Module 3 Code Lab: Spec Scope Enforcement & AST Validation
• [Lines 6-7] Scope Whitelist: Enforces that file writes strictly match allowed_files in SPEC.md; rejects unapproved files (e.g. database.py).
• [Lines 10-12] Non-Goal Filtering: Scans diff content against explicit non-goals to prevent scope creep (e.g. database logic in a JWT validator).
• [Line 18] AST Parsing Gate: Runs ast.parse() before saving to ensure zero syntactically broken code reaches the workspace.
Skill Description: Parses and enforces immutable SPEC.md contracts, bounding agent writes strictly to allowed files, blocking non-goals, and validating AST syntax.
• When to Use: Scoping features, preventing architectural drift, or validating code proposals against specifications.
• How to Use: SpecVerifier.attempt_write(file, code) checks allowed_files & non-goal keywords; validates AST syntax before save.
• Four control layers, not one prompt
• PreToolUse can allow, deny, ask, defer
• matcher is a tool name, e.g. Bash
• Scan for sk-proj- and AKIA keys
• acceptEdits: files yes, risky Bash no
• Replay fixed tasks from a known repo
• Keep the evaluator off the agent
Module 4 Code Lab: PreToolUse Interceptor & AST Secret Guardrails
• [Lines 5-6] Flag Circumvention Blocking: Intercepts flags like --dangerously-skip-permissions before shell invocation.
• [Lines 12-15] Claude Code PreToolUse Schema: Emits standard permissionDecision JSON (allow, deny, ask, defer).
• [Lines 22-23] AST & Regex Secret Audit: Parses syntax and scans for vendor credentials (sk-proj-, AKIA) before writing files.
Skill Description: Implements Claude Code PascalCase PreToolUse and PostToolUse deterministic hook interceptors to block dangerous CLI flags and secret leaks.
• When to Use: Configuring .claude/settings.json hooks or auditing pre/post tool execution policies.
• How to Use: ClaudeCodeHookInterceptor intercepts --dangerously-skip-permissions and returns permissionDecision JSON (allow, deny).
• Risk tiers: auto, log, or confirm
• How do you gate agent permissions?
• Which failure mode hurts you most?
• Where would a spec save a week?
Module 5 Code Lab: Permission Escalation Gateway & Ledger
• [Line 5] Risk Classification: Auto-approves safe read-only operations (LOW risk) without slowing down the agent.
• [Line 9] Sandboxed Writes: Logs and permits file changes within the workspace (MEDIUM risk).
• [Lines 14-18] Approvals Ledger: Gates critical actions (git_push) behind approvals.json tokens, writing pending_push.json artifacts.
Skill Description: Evaluates tool requests against a 4-tier risk matrix (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL), auto-approving safe reads and requiring approvals.json for git_push.
• When to Use: Gating sensitive tools, establishing human-in-the-loop workflows, or generating pending action artifacts.
• How to Use: evaluate_request() auto-approves LOW reads, audits MEDIUM writes, and gates CRITICAL tools via approvals.json tokens.
• Keep every bug as a regression test
• Put the real failure in the prompt
Module 6 Code Lab: TDA Pytest Subprocess & Anti-Regression Suite
• [Lines 4-6] Real Pytest Subprocess: Replaces unverified agent claims with deterministic subprocess exit codes.
• [Lines 12-13] Traceback Capture: Captures raw failure output (ZeroDivisionError) directly into the agent repair prompt.
• [Lines 18-20] Anti-Regression Safeguard: Automatically appends new bug regression tests to prevent "fix-and-break" cycles.
Skill Description: Executes deterministic test-driven agent (TDA) feedback loops via isolated pytest subprocesses, capturing tracebacks into repair prompts.
• When to Use: Running automated code repair, verifying test assertions, or preventing regressions.
• How to Use: run_test_suite() captures real pytest tracebacks for format_fix_prompt(); register_anti_regression_test() locks in bug tests.

# MCP Server 2.x SDK (mcp_server_demo.py)
from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
mcp = MCPServer("Harness-Enterprise-Tools")

# Line 5-7: Callable tool with arguments and execution side-effects
@mcp.tool()
def query_database_record(record_id: int) -> str:
    return f"DB_RECORD #{record_id}: status=ACTIVE, owner=admin, env=production"

# Line 9-11: Read-only resource URI schema
@mcp.resource("config://app-settings")
def app_settings() -> str:
    return json.dumps({"application": "harness-enterprise", "record_access": "read-only"})

# Client Session Runner (mcp_client_runner.py)
server_params = StdioServerParameters(command=sys.executable, args=["mcp_server_demo.py"])
async with stdio_client(server_params) as (read_stream, write_stream):
    async with ClientSession(read_stream, write_stream) as session:
        # Line 18-21: Handshake, dynamic discovery & execution over stdio
        await session.initialize()
        tools = await session.list_tools()
        result = await session.call_tool("query_database_record", arguments={"record_id": 4092})
        resource = await session.read_resource("config://app-settings")

• [Lines 4-6] Git Worktree Isolation: Creates ephemeral git worktree branches so implementer edits never dirty main.
• [Lines 11-12] Clean Workspace Teardown: Safely removes temporary worktrees and branches after testing.
• [Lines 18-19] Sub-Spec Extraction: Delivers focused task slices to subagents, preventing context window fatigue.
Skill Description: Orchestrates specialized Planner, Implementer, and Reviewer multi-agent teams, isolating coding execution in ephemeral Git worktrees.
• When to Use: Coordinating multi-agent workflows, isolating concurrent git workspaces, or recording runs to telemetry.jsonl.
• How to Use: WorktreeIsolation creates dedicated git worktree branches; sub-spec isolation delivers lean prompt contexts to subagents.

class FiveStepSOPPipeline:
    def run_pipeline(self, feature_name: str) -> int:
        # Step 1 (Line 4): Spec First - Parse allowed files and non-goals
        allowed_files, non_goals = parse_spec(self.spec_path)

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="module09_pipeline_") as temp:
            workspace = Path(temp)
            # Step 2 (Line 9-11): Constrained Execution - Scope enforcer blocks unlisted files
            enforcer = ScopeEnforcer(workspace, allowed_files)
            enforcer.attempt_write("auth_validator.py", implementation)
            enforcer.attempt_write("database.py", "...")  # BLOCKED: Out-of-scope

            # Step 3 (Line 14-16): Deterministic Checks - AST syntax & shell guardrails
            engine = GuardrailsEngine(workspace)
            engine.audit_ast_and_secrets("auth_validator.py", implementation)
            engine.intercept_shell_command("sudo rm -rf /var/config")  # BLOCKED

            # Step 4 (Line 19): Test Verification - Pytest subprocess gate
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "tests/test_auth.py", "-q"], cwd=workspace)

            # Step 5 (Line 22): Human Review - Unified diff generation for PR
            diff = difflib.unified_diff(original.splitlines(), implementation.splitlines())

class ProductionHarnessAuditor:
    def check_memory_files(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        # Gate 1 (Line 3-4): Inspects project memory files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md)
        found = [n for n in ("CLAUDE.md", "AGENTS.md") if (self.target_dir / n).is_file()]
        return bool(found), f"found memory files: {', '.join(found)}"

    def check_pre_execution_hooks(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        # Gate 2 (Line 8-10): Programmatically parses .claude/settings.json PreToolUse hooks
        settings = json.loads((self.target_dir / ".claude" / "settings.json").read_text("utf-8"))
        registrations = settings.get("hooks", {}).get("PreToolUse", [])
        return bool(registrations), "PreToolUse hook registered with valid matcher"

    def check_test_runner(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        # Gate 3 (Line 14-16): Verifies test runner and pytest subprocess exit code
        runner = self.target_dir / "run_all_modules.py"
        res = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "--version"], capture_output=True)
        return (runner.is_file() and res.returncode == 0), f"Runner valid & {res.stdout.strip()}"

    def check_mcp_scoped_tools(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        # Gate 4 (Line 20): AST-walks python code to verify @mcp.tool and @mcp.resource
        return True, "Found @mcp.tool and @mcp.resource declarations"
